If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.75) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings sharply (±0.5–1.0) over 3 consecutive days, adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect volatility decay.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope by 0.3–0.6% per day for early horizon to prevent momentum overextension.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase slope by 0.3–0.6% per day for mid horizon to prevent premature reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, cap forecast at +3% above recent high for late horizon to avoid inflationary drift.
